description: Shape 11 (lapack_dense_even512, 207ms, the SINGLE BIGGEST geomean term) is full-rank-flat -- every non-cluster dense approach is refuted (sign D&C no gap, Householder back-transform floor, subspace +-lambda degeneracy, Jacobi rotation cost, batched-reduction tail >= cuSOLVER at b640). The ONE un-refuted lever, independently surfaced by BOTH brief-10 and brief-11: the fused megakernel WINS n=448 b640 at 1.36x with NO batch floor, capped at n<=448 only by the 232KB SMEM limit. brief-10 VERIFIED thread-block clusters compile+run on this B200 (compute_100a, cudaLaunchKernelEx, distributed shared memory via map_shared_rank, -O2). Build a 2-CTA-cluster megakernel for n=512: distribute the packed-FP16 matrix + workspace across the 2 CTAs' DSMEM (2x232KB=464KB), row-distribute the tred2 tridiagonalization / tql2 QL / compact-WY back-transform across the cluster with cluster.sync() barriers and remote-DSMEM (map_shared_rank) reads for the cross-CTA symv/GEMM. Route the n=512 dense-majority shapes here -- shape 11 (lapdense_even, full spectrum), shape 3 (dense512), shape 6 (mixed512 dense subset) -- with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback so nothing regresses. The risk to measure and beat: remote-DSMEM latency in the distributed symv (brief-3 hit a symv bandwidth floor at n=512 with a NON-resident matrix; DSMEM keeps the whole matrix on-chip, which is the point). Forks best 12251fe so the win stacks with the megakernel inner-solve routing. -O2 not -O3, no 'stream' substring.

t1: 2-CTA cluster megakernel n=512, row-distributed packed-FP16 lower-tri across 2 CTAs DSMEM, scatter symv (local matrix reads only), cluster.sync barriers. CORRECT: 0/640 gate-fails on BOTH dense512 (shape3) AND lapack_dense_even512 (shape11); eigenvalues match cuSOLVER exactly; orth 4e-5, eigr 3e-6 vs 6e-3/1.2e-2 gates. Distributed algorithm SOUND. But 12x SLOWER: dense512 2110ms vs 171ms cuSOLVER. ncu (distributed symv/whole kernel): barrier-bound -- 39/50 cycles/instr stalled at CTA barrier (78%), Compute-SM 8%, occupancy 3% (SMEM 192KB/CTA -> 1 CTA/SM, cluster needs 2 SMs -> 74 max clusters), 510 columns x ~5 cluster.sync = ~2550 cluster barriers (each >> __syncthreads), branch-eff 27%. NOT a bandwidth floor (DRAM 0.03%) -- the scatter kept the matrix on-chip as designed; the loss is serialization+barrier overhead. Not routed (kernel compiled+validated standalone). Levers: cut cluster.sync count, reduce divergence, reconsider 2-CTA occupancy tradeoff.

t3: parametric C-CTA cluster (balanced pivot boundaries, global v/p staging) + __launch_bounds__(nt,2). DECISIVE occupancy diagnosis via ncu: occupancy was REGISTER-limited (Block Limit Registers=1, 128 regs/thread), NOT SMEM -- so C=4 shrinking SMEM to 64KB did NOT raise occupancy and was 2x SLOWER (4716ms) from added 4-way global-staging coordination. launch_bounds(,2) capped regs at 64/thread (no spills) -> Block Limit Registers=2, but SMEM now binds (C=2 balanced 128KB/CTA > 114KB -> Block Limit SharedMem=1, still 1 CTA/SM, 25% occ, 4 warps/sched, No-Eligible 92%). C=2+launch_bounds=1952ms (best cluster so far; C=2 no-lb 2111, C=4 4716). dense512 cuSOLVER=171ms so 11x off. All CORRECT 0/640. NEXT lever measured-necessary: C=3 (85KB<114KB) so reg AND SMEM both permit 2 CTAs/SM -> should ~2x occupancy. Deeper issue: per-column cross-CTA coordination overhead grows with C, fighting the megakernel's batch-parallel efficiency (640 indep CTAs).

t4-t5: NO-ATOMIC symmetric dot-product symv (each CTA computes p[i] for owned rows only; lower part local, upper part local rows + CTA0's remote-DSMEM reads of CTA1 rows via map_shared_rank) = 5x FASTER than atomic scatter (1952->393ms). t5 reverted a warp-per-row symv variant (439ms, warp-reduce overhead beat the conflict-free reads). BEST cluster: dense512 393ms=0.43x cuSOLVER(171), lapdense_even512 425ms=0.48x cuSOLVER(202); correct 0/640, orth 4e-5 eig 4e-6. ncu(t4): Compute-SM 28% Mem 38% (was 8/11), warp-cyc/instr 13(was 50), 532M shared-load bank conflicts (packed-tri), STILL 25% occupancy. KEY FINDING: C=2 occupancy is HARD-CAPPED at 25% (1 CTA/SM) because 2 CTAs holding the full n=512 FP16 matrix need 2x128KB>228KB physical SMEM -- theoretical min, C=3 hit a cluster-scheduling cliff (96ms/mat), C=4 2x slower coordination. remote-DSMEM did NOT reintroduce a bandwidth floor (DRAM 0.4%). Still ~2.3x off cuSOLVER; open levers: back-transform speedup (~70% share), bank-conflict-free rank-2/stage4, FP8 storage for occupancy (accuracy risk).

t7 (final, profiled): warp-shuffle reductions in cluster tridiag; DIRECT-DSMEM v/p exchange. FULL HARNESS: validate 39/39 PASS; benchmark geomean=41994us (clean). This +1.5% vs parent 41378 is ENTIRELY the mandated -O3--fast_math -> -O2 switch (per-shape numbers EXACTLY match brief-13's -O2: shape1 2809, shape3 113790, shape8 125402, shape12 47406) -- the cluster kernel is present but NOT routed (routing would regress: it is 0.43-0.51x cuSOLVER on shapes 3/6/11). Cluster kernel CORRECT 0/640 on ALL THREE targets: dense512(shape3) 0.44x, mixed512(shape6, heterogeneous) 0.43x, lapdense_even512(shape11) 0.48-0.51x. ncu trial7: 25% occ (hard cap), Compute-SM 26%, 532M shared-load bank conflicts (packed-tri reads), warp-cyc/instr 13. Stage split: tridiag 73%, back-transform 22%, solve 5%. remote-DSMEM symv is NOT a bandwidth floor (DRAM 0.4%). Ceiling = 25% occupancy (2x128KB FP16 matrix>228KB SMEM) + serial tridiag.

t8 (final committed clean state): removed the MEGA_EXTRA_CFLAGS diagnostic env hook (CLUST_SKIP_* stage-timing guards left inert). Behaviorally identical to t7. Committed submission = the 2-CTA cluster megakernel for n=512 (row-distributed packed-FP16, no-atomic symmetric dot-product symv with CTA0 remote-DSMEM reads of CTA1 rows, direct-DSMEM v/p exchange, warp-shuffle reductions, launch_bounds(512,2), sm_100a, -O2), PRESENT + CORRECT (0/640 on shapes 3/6/11 incl heterogeneous mixed512) + VALIDATED (39/39) but NOT ROUTED. benchmark geomean=41994us (parent 41378 + the mandated -O3->-O2 switch, +1.5%). Cluster is 0.43-0.51x cuSOLVER on n=512 dense shapes so routing would regress -> left un-routed. Full profile saved brief-14-trial-7-*.ncu-txt.

BUILT + BENCHMARKED a working 2-CTA thread-block-cluster megakernel for n=512 (the brief's milestone). It COMPILES + RUNS on this B200 (sm_100a, cudaLaunchKernelEx cluster-dim launch attr, cg::this_cluster + map_shared_rank DSMEM + cluster.sync, -O2) and is CORRECT across the full b640 batch on ALL THREE target shapes -- dense512(shape3), mixed512(shape6, heterogeneous), lapack_dense_even512(shape11) -- 0/640 gate-fails each, eigenvalues match cuSOLVER, orth 4e-5 / eig 4e-6 << the 6e-3/1.2e-2 gates. Design: row-distributed packed-FP16 lower-tri across CTAs; tred2 tridiag + Sturm/twisted solve + compact-WY back-transform distributed with cluster.sync; the symv is a NO-ATOMIC symmetric dot product (lower part local + CTA0 remote-DSMEM-reads CTA1's rows for the off-diagonal block -- the distributed symv the brief targeted). Kept present-but-UNROUTED (residual-gated wrapper _eigh_megakernel_clust512 exists) because it does not yet beat cuSOLVER; committed submission validates 39/39, benchmark 41994us (= parent 41378 + the mandated -O3->-O2 switch, +1.5%, per-shape EXACTLY matches brief-13's -O2).

MEASURED PROGRESSION (dense512 b640, cluster vs cuSOLVER 171ms): t1 atomic-scatter symv 2110ms(0.08x) -> t4 NO-ATOMIC dot+remote-DSMEM symv 393ms(0.43x, a 5.4x kernel speedup: the atomic scatter's ~67M SMEM atomics/matrix were the dominant cost) -> t7 +warp-shuffle reductions+direct-DSMEM exchange 387ms(0.44x). Final: dense512 0.44x, mixed512 0.43x, lapdense_even 0.48-0.51x.

THE CEILING (hard-measured, two independent walls): (1) OCCUPANCY hard-capped at 25% (1 CTA/SM): 2 CTAs each holding the full n=512 packed-FP16 matrix need 2x128KB=256KB > 228KB physical SMEM/SM -- theoretical minimum for a 2-CTA split. launch_bounds(,2) fixed the register cap (Block Limit Registers 1->2) but SMEM then binds. C=3 (85KB, would fit 2/SM) hit a CLUSTER-SCHEDULING CLIFF (96ms/matrix, 30x worse -- 3-CTA clusters don't co-reside efficiently on a GPC here); C=4 (64KB) was 2x slower from added global-staging coordination. (2) The TRIDIAGONALIZATION is 73% of the kernel (stage split via CLUST_SKIP macros: tridiag 288ms / back-transform 86ms / solve 19ms), serial over 510 columns with cluster.sync -- unlike single-CTA mega_eigh_med where back-transform is 70%. remote-DSMEM reads are NOT a bandwidth floor (DRAM 0.4%, the brief's key risk RULED OUT). 532M shared-load bank conflicts (packed-tri reads) remain.

CONCRETE OPEN DIRECTIONS (not pursued, all would need to beat BOTH walls): (a) BLOCKED/panel tridiagonalization -- replace 510 per-column symv+sync cycles with ~32 compact-WY panel-GEMM cycles, cutting the tridiag barrier count ~NBx (the 73% lever); big rewrite, still hits 25% occ. (b) FP8 matrix storage -- the ONLY path to <=114KB/CTA at C=2 (would DOUBLE occupancy to ~50%, matching mega_eigh_med); accuracy risk (brief-11 saw FP8 gate-fails) but the residual gate catches failures -- UNMEASURED here, worth a dedicated try since occupancy is the primary wall. (c) tensor-core (TF32/FP16) back-transform GEMMs (22%, currently FP32-SIMT). (d) bank-conflict-free swizzled/padded packed layout for the tridiag reads (532M conflicts). The cluster infra (parametric C via -DCLUST_C, balanced-pivot bounds, launch_bounds, DSMEM exchange) is all in place for (a)-(d) to build on.
